title: Main purpose of a literary excerpt or poem
subtitle: Text Structure and Purpose · 39 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **39 of the official questions in Text Structure and Purpose are this one** — 12 Easy, 16 Medium, 11 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The passage is introduced with 'The following text is from/adapted from [author's] [year] novel/poem/story/memoir,' often with a bracketed setup sentence.
- The question asks for the main purpose, and the choices start with 'To portray...,' 'To convey...,' 'To encourage...,' or 'To give an example of...'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Use the setup line to identify who the focus is (the narrator, a named character, or the addressee of the poem).
- 2) Say in plain words what the excerpt as a whole shows about that person, such as their reaction, a trait, a hope, or a feeling of being torn.
- 3) Pick the choice that names the right person and the right emotion or trait.
- Watch the tone: encouraging is not the same as warning.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Choices mention the right characters but shift the focus to the wrong person, for example the father's pride instead of the boy's wish.
Or they name a concrete detail the text never gives, like which topics were discussed or how the friends met.
In poems, a choice may reverse the tone, turning an encouraging poem into a warning or a lament.
Stick to what the excerpt as a whole conveys.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
Choices mention the right characters but shift the focus to the wrong person, for example the father's pride instead of the boy's wish.
Or they name a concrete detail the text never gives, like which topics were discussed or how the friends met.
